## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Fields implicits
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - IField evaluation and scalar/vector queries
//  - Differentiable field bodies
//  - Signed distance and membership queries
//  - Constant and function-valued field algebra
//  - Metaball influence and summation
//  - Flat node tree and graph accessors
//  - Sampled signed distance field lattice geometry
//  - Function-valued implicit shape algebra
//  - Marching squares — cell numbering, case table, kernel, driver, entry points
//  - Time-varying field bodies

library FieldsImplicits
{
    //==
    // # IField evaluation and scalar/vector queries
    //
    // Bodies for the root `IField` interface and the plain scalar and vector fields
    // declared in `fields.concepts.plato`. Every field inherits
    // `IProcedural<TDomain, TRange>`, whose sole operation is `Eval(x, input)`. The
    // generic `ValueAt` below names that evaluation for every field;
    // interface-specific helpers exist only where they carry semantic weight beyond
    // respelling Eval (sign and level-set queries, magnitude, flow direction). See
    // `README.md` for naming and unit conventions.

    //==
    // # IField<TDomain, TValue>
    //
    // The root spatial-field capability: a pure mapping from a domain position to
    // a value. Only `Eval` is available, so the single helper is a readable alias
    // that serves every field type — color, complex, tensor, vector, direction —
    // which is why those interfaces add no pure-evaluation alias of their own.

    // The field's value at a domain position; a readable spelling of Eval.
    ValueAt(self: IField<$TDomain, $TValue>, point: $TDomain): $TValue
        => self.Eval(point);

    //==
    // # IScalarField2D
    //
    // A real-valued field over the plane. Level-set membership and sign queries
    // are the natural derived surface over a bare scalar evaluation
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_set).
    // TODO(interface-gap): a numeric finite-difference gradient would need to sample
    // the field at points offset from `point`, but no sanctioned Point2D offset
    // operation is in scope here (IDifference.Add needs a Vector2D that ICoordinate
    // cannot supply); use IDifferentiableScalarField2D for gradients instead.

    // True where the field is strictly positive at the point. Note: values within
    // rounding of zero classify by sign noise; use IsNearLevelAt for a balanced,
    // tolerance-based test around a level.
    IsPositiveAt(self: IScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) > 0.0;

    // True where the field is strictly negative at the point. Note: near-zero
    // values classify by sign noise; use IsNearLevelAt around zero for balance.
    IsNegativeAt(self: IScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) < 0.0;

    // True where the field's value at the point is at or above level: the closed
    // super-level-set membership test { p : field(p) >= level }.
    IsAtOrAboveLevel(self: IScalarField2D, point: Point2D, level: Number): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) >= level;

    // True where the field's value at the point is within tolerance of level: a
    // balanced test for the level set. Precondition: tolerance is non-negative.
    IsNearLevelAt(self: IScalarField2D, point: Point2D, level: Number, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => (self.Eval(point) - level).Abs <= tolerance;

    //==
    // # IScalarField3D
    //
    // A real-valued field over space. Mirrors the planar sign and level-set
    // queries above.

    // True where the field is strictly positive at the point. Note: near-zero
    // values classify by sign noise; prefer IsNearLevelAt for a balanced test.
    IsPositiveAt(self: IScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) > 0.0;

    // True where the field is strictly negative at the point. Note: near-zero
    // values classify by sign noise; prefer IsNearLevelAt for a balanced test.
    IsNegativeAt(self: IScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) < 0.0;

    // True where the field's value at the point is at or above level: the closed
    // super-level-set membership test.
    IsAtOrAboveLevel(self: IScalarField3D, point: Point3D, level: Number): Boolean
        => self.Eval(point) >= level;

    // True where the field's value at the point is within tolerance of level.
    // Precondition: tolerance is non-negative.
    IsNearLevelAt(self: IScalarField3D, point: Point3D, level: Number, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => (self.Eval(point) - level).Abs <= tolerance;

    //==
    // # IVectorField2D
    //
    // A planar vector field. Evaluation itself is the generic ValueAt; the helpers
    // here project the sampled vector to scalar and direction summaries.

    // The length of the sampled vector: flow speed or displacement magnitude.
    MagnitudeAt(self: IVectorField2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => self.Eval(point).Magnitude;

    // The unit flow direction of the sampled vector. Precondition: the field is
    // non-zero at the point.
    FlowDirectionAt(self: IVectorField2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.Eval(point).Normalize;

    //==
    // # IVectorField3D
    //
    // A spatial vector field. Mirrors the planar magnitude and flow-direction
    // helpers.

    // The length of the sampled vector: flow speed or displacement magnitude.
    MagnitudeAt(self: IVectorField3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.Eval(point).Magnitude;

    // The unit flow direction of the sampled vector. Precondition: the field is
    // non-zero at the point.
    FlowDirectionAt(self: IVectorField3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.Eval(point).Normalize;
```
